obligation: Call emergency responders for any fire or release
trigger: Fire, chemical release, or exothermic reaction in T-1 or T-2, whatever the cause
deadline: At once, before any other call
notify: 911 (county fire rescue); the company does not perform hazmat response
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - company rule; the county fire department walks through the plan each year

obligation: CERCLA release notice to the National Response Center
trigger: Release of a hazardous substance at or above its RQ in any 24-hour period. Sodium hydroxide RQ 1,000 lb (count the NaOH content, 302.6(b)(1)(i): about 2,000 lb or 157 gal of 50% solution); sodium hypochlorite RQ 100 lb (about 800 lb or 80 gal of 12.5% solution); phosphoric acid RQ 5,000 lb (more than one full tote). Hydrogen peroxide and isopropyl alcohol are not CERCLA hazardous substances
deadline: Immediately, as soon as the person in charge knows of the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - regardless of cause (cyber or not); printed call list with RQs in gallons (POAM-012)

obligation: EPCRA emergency release notice (immediate)
trigger: Release of a CERCLA hazardous substance at or above its RQ that could expose people beyond the property line. Releases that expose persons solely within the facility boundaries are exempt (355.31(a))
deadline: Immediately
notify: LEPC community emergency coordinator and the SERC of any state likely to be affected
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if people outside the site could be exposed

obligation: EPCRA written follow-up notice
trigger: After an immediate EPCRA notice for a release at the facility (not required for a release during transportation, 355.40(c))
deadline: As soon as practicable after the release
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an immediate EPCRA notice was made

obligation: DOT immediate telephone notice of a hazmat incident
trigger: During transportation in commerce, including loading, unloading, and temporary storage: as a direct result of a hazardous material a person is killed or admitted to a hospital, the public is evacuated for 1 hour or more, or a major transportation artery is closed for 1 hour or more; or a continuing danger to life exists in the judgment of the person in possession
deadline: As soon as practical and no later than 12 hours after the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the incident involves packaged product in transportation while in the company's physical possession, for example a dropped tote while loading a carrier's trailer in the driver's presence (49 CFR 171.8, loading incidental to movement). Not triggered by an incident in the blend room

obligation: DOT written hazardous materials incident report
trigger: Any 171.15 incident, or any unintentional release of a hazardous material during transportation (including loading, unloading, and temporary storage). Exception for small releases of Packing Group III Class 8 or Class 3 material from packages under 20 L (171.16(d)(2))
deadline: Within 30 days of discovery; keep a copy 2 years
applies_at_this_tier: Only for a transportation incident in the company's physical possession (same test as 171.15)

obligation: OSHA severe injury and fatality report
trigger: Work-related fatality; in-patient hospitalization of an employee; amputation; or loss of an eye (for example a chemical burn from a manipulated batch)
deadline: Fatality within 8 hours; hospitalization, amputation, or eye loss within 24 hours
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the 10-employee partial exemption covers injury records only; every covered employer must report under 1904.39 (1904.1(a)(1))

obligation: Voluntary cyber incident report
citation: CISA and FBI voluntary reporting; CISA RBPS 8 guidance (C-CHEMICAL-R01, voluntary benchmark); POL-03 4.8
trigger: Suspected or confirmed intrusion into the batch control system
deadline: No legal deadline; company target within 24 hours of declaration (POL-03 4.8)
notify: CISA (incident reporting form reached from cisa.gov/report) and the FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary - recommended; also a mitigating factor for OFAC

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected intrusion, ransomware, data theft, or extortion demand
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring any outside firm; use panel counsel and forensics
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: General liability and pollution liability claim notice
citation: General liability and pollution liability policies (contract); POL-03 4.6
trigger: Anyone hurt, a release, or property damage, because the cyber policy excludes bodily injury and property damage
deadline: Per each policy's notice clause
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: MSP and integrator incident notice to the company (inbound)
citation: MSP contract and integrator service agreement (POL-02 A.5; POAM-013)
trigger: The MSP or integrator detects a security incident affecting company systems or its own tools and accounts
deadline: Target in new terms: within 24 hours. Today neither contract has an incident notice term
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual - not yet in either contract; due 2026-12-31

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (employee personal information)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents, for example payroll or HR files taken from the office computers or the shared drive
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15-day extension only for good cause given in writing to the Department within 30 days)
notify: Affected Florida residents (current and former employees)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if employee personal information was accessed; none is held on the HMI PC or the PLC

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in its written request
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: No - 7 employees and a small number of former employees

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: No - far below the count

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains employee personal information for the company (payroll service, productivity suite, MSP) has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination (vendor duty)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm in the payroll vendor terms (R-022)

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected employees or former employees who live outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected people

obligation: CFATS significant security incident report (RBPS 15)
trigger: Significant security incident at a covered facility
deadline: Not enforceable
applies_at_this_tier: No - CFATS authority terminated in July 2023 and was not reauthorized as of 2026-10-05; the facility was never tiered; report voluntarily to CISA instead

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident report / ransom payment report (PROPOSED - not yet in effect)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours after reasonable belief; 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - no final rule as of 2026-10-05; as proposed the company is under the SBA size criterion and the CFATS sector criterion is moot

obligation: Reporting of actual or threatened cyber incidents at MTSA facilities / OCS facilities / vessels
trigger: Cyber incident at an MTSA-regulated facility
deadline: Immediately (6.16-1); without delay to the National Response Center
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Coast Guard Captain of the Port; or National Response Center
applies_at_this_tier: No - inland unit with no marine transfer; not a 33 CFR Part 105 facility

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
